comparison_axes.250k_vs_500k_vs_1m: Flat ladders often degraded after 250k; hierarchical exact-resume ladder preserved pass status at 250k, 500k, and 1M.
comparison_axes.exact_resume_off_vs_on: V2.4 legacy continuation exposed the empty replay/RNG bug; V2.5 exact resume improved premium/high-holding/route dispatch-success but still failed 500k, proving exact resume is necessary but not sufficient.
comparison_axes.flat_dqn_vs_hierarchical_v1: Flat 48-action DQN repeatedly shifted into composite action pockets (32/33/41/45/46), while hierarchical_v1 passed 250k/500k/1M and equal-budget assurance.
comparison_axes.public_route_validation: Amazon/OR-Tools route benchmarks support route-side plausibility only and cannot validate fleet or reorder economics.
comparison_axes.reward_patch_vs_architecture: Reward/config patches repaired local pockets but failures migrated; architecture-level action factorization addressed the repeated failure pattern more robustly.
comparison_axes.teacher_retention_vs_hierarchical: Teacher retention failed at 250k despite active retention telemetry; hierarchical_v1 then passed the full ladder, making hierarchical architecture the stronger causal fix.

limitations: Some branches differ in reward/config and chronology, so causal claims are evidence-weighted rather than strictly isolated.
overall_conclusion: The strongest causal story is cumulative: exact resume fixed a real continuation bug, but the decisive product-quality improvement came from hierarchical_v1 action factorization plus flat-teacher distillation and exact-resume laddering. Further blind training is not recommended without a monitored trigger or company-data mismatch.
scope: Historical ablation-style synthesis from existing artifacts only; no fresh ablation training.
